Insurance Risk – The risk that the claims and premium liabilities esti- mated are higher than actual claims that the company ends up settling. Life Insurance • Longevity • Persistency • Mortality and Morbidity • Expenses Health Insurance • Underwriting • Expenses • Reserving We take measured amounts on both life and health insurance risks in line with our core skills in underwriting and pricing. Effective underwriting and reinsurance strategies mitigate exposure to claim volatility and catastrophic events. Additional supporting structures include: • Robust product development frameworks which generate products that meet customer needs. • Rollout of policyholder engagements and retention strategies. • Extensive use of data and financial models to improve pricing. • Implementation of robust expense management initiatives. • Retention of additional capital, guided by Risk Based Capital (RBC) guidelines, that shield the company against this risk.

data.item: Liquidity & Capital Adequacy Risk – Risk that the business cannot meet its obligations as and when they fall due. • Mismatch of assets and liabilities, usually by duration and amounts. • Low generation of cashflow. Might be due to reduced inflows and elevated withdrawals. Stringent liquidity and capital management practices ensure that JHL can meet its financial obligations under stressed scenarios. They include: • Asset Liability Matching (ALM) policy that ensures as- sets and labilities are matched by amounts, currency, duration and nature. • Contingency funding plan to be put in place to ad- dress funding requirements in stressed scenarios. • Holding sufficient capital buffers above regulatory minimums.

data.item: Counterparty and Credit Risks – Risks that counterparties may not be able to pay their ongoing obligations, including inability to convert investments to cash despite having a legal obligation to do so. • Premium receivables • Reinsurance exposures – i.e. reinsurers share of liabilities, outstanding claims and commissions • Bank deposits • Corporate bonds and commercial papers • Internal credit policy of cash and carry for retail customers coupled with a maximum of 60 days for corporate credit. Additionally, provisions are made as per IFRS 9 guidelines. • Risk appetite limit that all reinsurance cessions are made with parties that have a credit rating of at least A- (by an Internationally recognised rating agency) • Risk appetite limits for exposure to corporate bonds and commercial papers.
